subject: Culture
title: The Golden Ratio in Temples
description: A fast breakdown of The Golden Ratio in Temples for builders.

hook.text: The Parthenon's facade fits a golden rectangle so precisely that mathematicians still debate if it was intentional.

buildup.text: The golden ratio—approximately 1.618—appears in shells, galaxies, and ancient architecture alike.

discovery.text: Hindu temples use the 'vastu purusha mandala,' a sacred grid that maps a cosmic being onto the floor plan.

twist.text: Many 'golden ratio' claims are retroactive. Builders often used simpler proportions that look similar by coincidence.

climax.text: Whether intentional or accidental, proportioned spaces consistently rate higher in beauty studies.

punchline.text: Sacred geometry works even on non-believers.

quiz.question: What is the approximate value of the golden ratio?
